questions.question: What is the prize money for Bal Sahitya Puraskar winners?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹50,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** is a prestigious literary honor in **India**, instituted by the **Sahitya Akademi**, which is the **National Academy of Letters**.
 
• The prize money for the **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** winners consists of a **casket** containing an engraved **copper-plaque** and a cheque of **₹50,000**. ***Hence, the correct answer is ₹50,000.***
 
• This award was established in the year **2010** to recognize and promote excellence in **children’s literature** across various Indian languages.
 
• The awards are presented annually for the most outstanding books by **Indian authors**, first published during the **five years** immediately preceding the year of the award.
 
• The selection of the awardees is made on the basis of recommendations made by **Juries** comprising **three members** in the respective languages, following the procedure laid down for the purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Main Award:**
 
 
• The main **Sahitya Akademi Award** is given to the most outstanding books of literary merit published in any of the major Indian languages.
 
• The prize money for the main award was initially **₹5,000** in **1954**, which was later increased to **₹1,00,000** from the year **2009** onwards.
 
 
 
• **Yuva Puraskar:**
 
 
• The **Yuva Puraskar** was instituted in **2011** to encourage young writers under the **age of 35**.
 
• Similar to the Bal Sahitya Puraskar, the prize money for the **Yuva Puraskar** is also **₹50,000** and an engraved **copper-plaque**.
 
 
 
• **Languages Recognized:**
 
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** recognizes **24 languages** for its awards.
 
• These include the **22 languages** listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, along with **English** and **Rajasthani**.
 
 
 
• **Translation Prize:**
 
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi Translation Prize** is given to outstanding translations of creative and critical works.
 
• The amount of this prize is also **₹50,000**, aimed at facilitating cross-cultural literary exchange within **India**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Establishment of Sahitya Akademi:** The **Sahitya Akademi** was formally inaugurated by the **Government of India** on **12 March 1954**. It functions as an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**.
 
• **Headquarters:** The headquarters of the Akademi is located in **Rabindra Bhavan**, **New Delhi**, which also houses other national academies like Sangeet Natak Akademi and Lalit Kala Akademi.
 
• **Bhasha Samman:** Apart from the regular annual awards, the Akademi gives **Bhasha Samman** to writers/scholars for significant contribution to **classical** and **medieval literature** and languages not formally recognized by the Akademi. The prize money for Bhasha Samman is **₹1,00,000**.
 
• **Eligibility of Books:** To be eligible for the **Bal Sahitya Puraskar**, the book must be a work of **original writing** for children and not a translation or an edited work.

questions.question: The share of ULIPs in the total APE of which insurance company fell to 46.8% in Q1 FY26, compared to 51.4% in the same quarter last year?

options.text: Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance Co. Ltd.
Axis Max Life Insurance Co. Ltd.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICICI Prudential Life Insurance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The share of **Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs)** in the total **Annualized Premium Equivalent (APE)** for **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance** witnessed a decrease to **46.8%** during the **first quarter (Q1)** of **FY26**.
 
• This is a notable decline from the **51.4%** share recorded in the **same quarter of the previous financial year (Q1 FY25)**, indicating a shift in the company's product distribution strategy. ***Hence, the correct answer is ICICI Prudential Life Insurance.***
 
• The reduction in **ULIP** concentration suggests a strategic move by the insurer to diversify its portfolio by increasing the focus on **non-linked savings** and **protection** products.
 
• **ICICI Prudential** has been actively rebalancing its mix to mitigate risks associated with equity market volatility, which directly impacts the demand and performance of **market-linked products** like **ULIPs**.
 
• Despite the lower share of **ULIPs**, the company continues to maintain a strong market position by leveraging its multi-channel distribution network, including **bancassurance** and **agency** channels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Annualized Premium Equivalent (APE):**

 
 
• **APE** is a standardized measure used by the insurance industry to compare sales across different periods. It is calculated as the **sum of 100% of regular premiums** and **10% of single premiums** received during the year.
 
• It helps analysts and investors understand the growth trajectory of an insurance firm regardless of the premium payment frequency chosen by customers.
 
 
 
• **Unit Linked Insurance Plans (ULIPs):**
 
 
• A **ULIP** is a financial product that offers a combination of **insurance** and **investment**. A portion of the premium is used for life cover, while the remainder is invested in **equity, debt, or hybrid funds**.
 
• These plans are subject to **market risks**, and the **Net Asset Value (NAV)** fluctuates based on the performance of the underlying assets.
 
 
 
• **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited:**
 
 
• It is a joint venture between **ICICI Bank Limited** and **Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited**.
 
• The company commenced its operations in **2001** and was the **first private sector life insurer** in India to be listed on the **National Stock Exchange (NSE)** and **Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE)** in **2016**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai, Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:**
 
 
• The insurance sector in India is regulated by the **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)**, which was established under the **IRDA Act, 1999**.
 
• **IRDAI** ensures the protection of policyholders' interests and regulates the **solvency margins** and **investment norms** for insurance companies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leadership:** As of recent filings, **Anup Bagchi** serves as the **Managing Director & CEO** of **ICICI Prudential Life Insurance**.
 
• **Value of New Business (VNB):** This is a key metric for life insurers that represents the **present value of future profits** expected from the new business written during a specific period. A diversified product mix often aims to improve the **VNB margin**.
 
• **Solvency Ratio:** It is a measure of an insurance company's ability to meet its long-term claims. **IRDAI** mandates a minimum **solvency ratio of 150%** to ensure financial stability.
 
• **Market Trends:** The shift away from **ULIPs** toward **guaranteed return plans** often occurs when interest rates are favorable or when investors seek **capital protection** over high-risk market returns.

questions.question: India submitted its 4th Biennial Update Report to the UNFCCC in December 2024. What is the full form of UNFCCC?

options.text: Union Network for Future Climate Control
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Foundation for Climate Cooperation
United Nations Forum for Climate Coordination

questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **UNFCCC** stands for the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change**, which is the primary international treaty aimed at addressing **climate change**.
 
• The convention was adopted on **9 May 1992** and opened for signature at the **Rio Earth Summit** (United Nations Conference on Environment and Development) in **June 1992**.
 
• Its ultimate objective is to achieve the **stabilization of greenhouse gas concentrations** in the atmosphere at a level that would prevent dangerous anthropogenic interference with the **climate system**.
 
• India, as a party to the convention, submitted its **4th Biennial Update Report (BUR)** in **December 2024**. This report provides updates on the **national greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory**, mitigation actions, and the support needed and received.
 
• The **UNFCCC Secretariat** is located in **Bonn, Germany**, and it supports the global response to the threat of climate change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure and Membership**:
 
 
• The **UNFCCC** has near-universal membership, with **198 Parties** having ratified the convention.
 
• The **Conference of the Parties (COP)** is the supreme decision-making body of the Convention, meeting **annually** to assess progress in dealing with climate change.
 
• Parties are classified into **Annex I** (industrialized countries), **Annex II** (developed countries that provide financial resources), and **Non-Annex I** (mostly developing countries, including **India**).
 
 
 
• **Key International Agreements**:
 
 
• The **Kyoto Protocol**, adopted in **1997**, was the first major extension of the UNFCCC, setting legally binding emission reduction targets for **developed countries**.
 
• The **Paris Agreement**, adopted in **2015** at **COP21**, aims to limit **global warming** to well below **2 degrees Celsius**, preferably to **1.5 degrees Celsius**, compared to pre-industrial levels.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Mechanisms**:
 
 
• **Biennial Update Reports (BURs)** are submitted by **Non-Annex I** parties every **two years** to maintain transparency regarding their climate actions and **carbon footprint**.
 
• Under the **Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF)** of the Paris Agreement, these reports are transitioning into **Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs)** to ensure more rigorous tracking of **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India's Climate Commitments**:
 
 
• India has pledged to achieve **Net Zero emissions** by the year **2070**, as announced at **COP26** in **Glasgow**.
 
• In its updated **NDCs**, India aims to reduce the **emission intensity** of its GDP by **45%** by **2030** from **2005 levels**.
 
• India is also working toward achieving **50% cumulative electric power** installed capacity from **non-fossil fuel-based energy** resources by **2030**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 4th BUR (2024)**:
 
 
• The **4th BUR** submitted in **December 2024** highlights India's progress in decoupling its **economic growth** from **greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The report includes data on sectors such as **Energy**, **Industrial Processes and Product Use (IPPU)**, **Agriculture**, **Waste**, and **Land Use, Land-Use Change, and Forestry (LULUCF)**.

questions.question: Where was the VLSRSAM flight-test conducted by DRDO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Integrated Test Range, Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vertical Launch Short Range Surface-to-Air Missile (VL-SRSAM)** was successfully flight-tested by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** and the **Indian Navy**.
 
• The test was conducted from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)**, **Chandipur**, off the coast of **Odisha**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• The **VL-SRSAM** is an indigenous weapon system designed to neutralize various aerial threats at close ranges, including **sea-skimming targets**.
 
• During the test, the missile was launched from a **naval ship** against a high-speed unmanned aerial target to demonstrate its vertical launch capability.
 
• The system has been developed by **DRDO** facilities, primarily the **Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)** and **Research Centre Imarat (RCI)** based in **Hyderabad**, but the physical testing occurred at the **Odisha** range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR), Odisha:**
 
 
• Located at **Chandipur** in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, it serves as the primary missile testing facility for **India**.
 
• It provides the necessary infrastructure for the performance evaluation of rockets, missiles, and airborne weapon systems.
 
• Most of India's major missiles, including the **Agni**, **Prithvi**, and **Akash** series, have been tested here.
 
 
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• It was established in **1958** by merging the Technical Development Establishment of the **Indian Army** and the Directorate of Technical Development and Production.
 
• It functions under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India, and is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• The current Chairman of **DRDO** (as of 2024) is **Dr. Samir V Kamat**.
 
 
 
• **VL-SRSAM Technical Specifications:**
 
 
• It is a **canisterized** system, which means it is stored and operated from specially designed compartments.
 
• The missile has a strike range of approximately **40 to 50 km** and can hit targets at an altitude of around **15 km**.
 
• It features **cruciform wings** that provide aerodynamic stability and **thrust vector control** for high maneuverability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Overview:**
 
 
• **Pokhran Test Range, Rajasthan:** This site is primarily used for testing **artillery guns** and was the location for India's **nuclear tests** in **1974** and **1998**.
 
• **Surya Lanka, Andhra Pradesh:** This is a station for the **Indian Air Force** located in **Bapatla**, often used for live-fire exercises of Surface-to-Air Missiles like **Akash**.
 
• **DRDO Missile Complex, Hyderabad:** This is a major research hub comprising **DRDL**, **RCI**, and **Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL)** where missiles are **designed** and **developed**, rather than being the primary site for long-range flight testing.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The successful development of **VL-SRSAM** enhances the **Indian Navy's** defensive capabilities against supersonic anti-ship missiles. It replaces the older **Barak-1** surface-to-air missile systems on Indian warships.
</ul

questions.question: The 2025 French Open, also known as Roland Garros, was played on which type of court surface?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clay Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **French Open**, also popularly known as **Roland Garros**, is unique among the four **Grand Slam** tennis tournaments as it is the only one played on **Clay Courts**.
 
• The **2025** edition of the tournament is scheduled to be held in **Paris**, **France**, at the iconic **Stade Roland Garros**, maintaining its long-standing tradition of using "**Terre Battue**" (red clay).
 
• The surface is characterized by its **slow speed** and **high bounce**, which significantly alters the dynamics of the game compared to other surfaces. It rewards players with great **stamina**, **patience**, and the ability to **slide** into shots. ***Hence, the option Clay Court is correct.***
 
• Historically, the tournament transitioned to its current location in **1928**, and the **2025** event continues to be managed by the **French Tennis Federation (FFT)**.
 
• Because the surface slows down the ball and makes it harder to hit unreturnable serves (aces), the **French Open** is often considered the most **physically demanding** tennis tournament in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Surface Composition:**
 
 
• A **French Open** clay court is not made of pure clay; it is actually a **five-layer structure**. The top layer consists of **1-2 mm** of **crushed red brick**, followed by **crushed limestone**, **clinker** (coal residue), **crushed gravel**, and finally a **drainage system**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Surfaces:**
 
 
• **Grass Courts:** These are used at **Wimbledon** in the **United Kingdom**. It is the **fastest** surface with a **low bounce**. ***Hence, the option Grass is incorrect.***
 
• **Hard Courts:** Used at the **Australian Open** and the **US Open**. These are made of **synthetic/acrylic** layers over **concrete** or **asphalt**, providing a **medium-fast** pace. ***Hence, the option Hard Court is incorrect.***
 
• **Artificial Turf:** While used in some local or recreational clubs, it is never used for professional **Grand Slam** level events. ***Hence, the option Artificial Turf is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The tournament was first held in **1891** as a national championship. It opened to international players in **1925**. It is named after the **French aviator** **Roland Garros**, who was the first person to fly across the **Mediterranean Sea**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The King of Clay:** **Rafael Nadal** of **Spain** holds the record for the most men's singles titles at the **French Open**, having won **14 titles** as of recent years. His dominance on this surface is unprecedented in sports history.
 
• **Championship Format:** The tournament features **Men’s Singles** (best of **five sets**), **Women’s Singles** (best of **three sets**), as well as **Doubles** and **Mixed Doubles**.
 
• **Prize Money and Ranking:** As a **Grand Slam**, the event offers the highest possible **ATP** and **WTA** ranking points (**2000 points** for the winner) and multi-million **Euro** prize purses.
 
• **Environmental Factors:** Because it is an **outdoor** tournament played on a natural surface, weather conditions like **humidity** and **wind** play a significant role. Damp weather makes the clay heavier and slower, while hot, dry weather makes it faster and the bounce higher.

questions.question: Which team won the National Team of the Year award at the Sportstar Aces Awards 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Chess Teams**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Chess Teams** (both Men and Women) were crowned the **National Team of the Year** at the prestigious **Sportstar Aces Awards 2025** held in **Mumbai**.
 
• This recognition was primarily due to their historic "Double Gold" achievement at the **45th FIDE Chess Olympiad** held in **Budapest**, **Hungary**, in **September 2024**.
 
• The **Men's team**, comprising **Gukesh D**, **R Praggnanandhaa**, **Arjun Erigaisi**, **Vidit Gujrathi**, and **Pentala Harikrishna**, finished at the top of the open section with an almost perfect score.
 
• The **Women's team**, consisting of **Harika Dronavalli**, **R Vaishali**, **Divya Deshmukh**, **Vantika Agrawal**, and **Tania Sachdev**, also secured the **Gold Medal**, marking the first time India won both categories simultaneously.
 
• The performance solidified India's position as a global superpower in chess, with players like **Gukesh D** and **Arjun Erigaisi** also winning individual gold medals for their respective boards. ***Hence, the correct answer is Indian Chess Teams.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sportstar Aces Awards:** 
 
 
• It is an annual awards ceremony organized by **The Hindu Group** through its sports magazine, **Sportstar**.
 
• The **2025 edition** celebrated the sporting achievements of Indian athletes throughout the calendar year **2024**, which included the **Paris Olympics** and **Paralympics**.
 
 
 
• **Other Major Winners in 2025:**
 
 
• **Sportstar of the Year (Male):** **Gukesh D** was honored for his stellar year, which included winning the **Candidates Tournament** and leading the Olympiad team.
 
• **Sportstar of the Year (Female):** **Manu Bhaker** received this award after becoming the first Indian in the post-Independence era to win **two medals** in a single edition of the **Olympics** (Paris 2024).
 
• **Sportsman of the Year (Track and Field):** **Neeraj Chopra** was recognized for his **Silver Medal** at the **Paris 2024 Olympics**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the 45th Chess Olympiad:**

• The **‘Cyber Suraksha’** exercise serves as a collaborative platform for the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, and **Indian Air Force** to develop **jointness** and **synergy** in their cyber operations.
 
• A primary objective of this drill is to test the robustness of the **military’s information technology infrastructure** and ensure the security of **strategic communication networks** against potential **cyber-espionage** and **state-sponsored attacks**.

questions.question: What was the theme of the International Day of Democracy, 2025, celebrated in September 2025?

options.text: Achieving Gender Equality, Action by Action

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Achieving Gender Equality, Action by Action**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Day of Democracy** is celebrated annually on **September 15** across the globe to promote and uphold the principles of **democracy**.
 
• For the year **2025**, the designated theme is **Achieving Gender Equality, Action by Action**, focusing on the critical role that **gender parity** plays in the sustainability of democratic institutions.
 
• The day was established by a resolution passed by the **United Nations General Assembly** in **2007**, with the aim of encouraging governments to strengthen their **national programs** devoted to the promotion and consolidation of democracy.
 
• The theme **Achieving Gender Equality, Action by Action** highlights that a **democracy** is truly representative only when **women** have equal access to **political leadership** and decision-making processes. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 4.***
 
• This theme emphasizes **concrete actions** and **policy reforms** rather than just rhetoric, aiming to eliminate the **systemic barriers** that prevent **marginalized genders** from participating in **civic life**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The idea for the day originated from the **Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU)**, which adopted the **Universal Declaration on Democracy** in **September 1997**.
 
• This declaration affirmed that **democracy** is an **international standard** and a fundamental right for all citizens of the world.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**
 
 
• The **2025 theme** is closely linked to **SDG 5** (**Gender Equality**) and **SDG 16** (**Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions**).
 
• The **United Nations** recognizes that **inclusive governance** is essential for achieving the **2030 Agenda** for Sustainable Development.
 
 
 
• **Legal Foundations:**
 
 
• The principles of **democracy** are enshrined in the **Universal Declaration of Human Rights**, specifically under **Article 21**, which states that the **will of the people** shall be the basis of the authority of government.
 
• This is expressed through **periodic and genuine elections** by universal and **equal suffrage**.
 
 
 
• **Global Participation:**
 
 
• Various **non-governmental organizations (NGOs)**, **parliaments**, and **civil society** groups hold events on **September 15** to discuss **transparency**, **accountability**, and **human rights**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gender and Democracy:** Research by the **UN Women** and the **IPU** consistently shows that countries with higher **female representation** in **legislatures** tend to pass more laws related to **social welfare**, **education**, and **healthcare**.
 
• **Challenges in 2025:** The theme addresses the **global decline** in democratic freedoms in some regions and the **gender-based violence** that often targets women in **public office**.
 
• **Implementation:** **"Action by Action"** refers to localized efforts such as **legislative quotas**, **funding for women candidates**, and **combating online harassment** to ensure a safe **democratic space** for all.
 
• **Institutional Role:** The **United Nations Department of Global Communications** works alongside the **IPU** to disseminate educational materials about the **rule of law** and **voter education** on this day.
</ul

questions.question: In 2025, which authority raised serious objections to the Aparajita Bill 2024, calling its proposed punishments under BNS excessively harsh and disproportionate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Government** of India, primarily through the **Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**, raised serious objections in early **2025** regarding the **Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024**.
 
• The **Aparajita Bill** was passed by the **West Bengal Legislative Assembly** on **September 3, 2024**, in the aftermath of the **RG Kar Medical College** incident to strengthen laws against sexual violence.
 
• The **Central Government** argued that the proposed punishments under the bill were **excessively harsh and disproportionate** compared to the provisions laid out in the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, which replaced the Indian Penal Code. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• A major point of contention was the bill's provision for a **mandatory death penalty** in cases of rape where the victim dies or is left in a vegetative state, which the **Central Government** noted deviates from the discretionary power given to judges under the **BNS 2023**.
 
• The **Central Government** emphasized that since "Criminal Law" falls under the **Concurrent List** of the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, any state amendment that is repugnant to a Central law requires **Presidential assent** under **Article 254(2)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Aparajita Bill, 2024:**
 
 
• The bill officially titled the **Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024**, seeks to amend the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and the **POCSO Act** in their application to **West Bengal**.
 
• Key features include a **10-day investigation limit** for rape cases from the date of the preliminary report and the creation of a specialized **Aparajita Task Force** at the district level.
 
• The bill proposes **rigorous imprisonment** for life for the remainder of the convict's natural life without parole for various categories of sexual assault.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS):**
 
 
• The **BNS** is the official criminal code of India, which came into effect on **July 1, 2024**, replacing the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**.
 
• It contains **358 sections** and introduces new offenses like **terrorism**, **organized crime**, and **mob lynching**, while enhancing punishments for crimes against women and children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Repugnancy:** Under **Article 254**, if any provision of a law made by the Legislature of a State is **repugnant** to any provision of a law made by Parliament, the Central law prevails unless the State law has received the **assent of the President**.
 
• **Procedural Hurdles:** The **West Bengal Governor** referred the **Aparajita Bill** to the **President of India** for consideration, leading to the **Ministry of Home Affairs** scrutinizing it for legal and procedural consistency with existing national frameworks.
 
• **Legal Criticism:** Legal experts have noted that **mandatory capital punishment** has been previously struck down by the **Supreme Court** in cases like **Mithu vs. State of Punjab (1983)**, as it violates **Articles 14 and 21** of the Constitution by removing judicial discretion.
</ul
